title: Finite rows and the abutment comparison
statement:
Let $\square$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g':X'\to X$, and let $\Ex_\square:g^{-1}Rf_*\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}$ be the derived exchange transformation [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] of functors $\Dplus(X_{\Et})\to\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $\Phi=g^{-1}Rf_*$ and $\Phi'=Rf'_*g'^{-1}$. Let $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ and $a\in\mathbf Z$ with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$, and let $(D,E)$ and $(D',E')$ be the two exact couples of [def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples], obtained by applying $\Phi$ and $\Phi'$ to the truncation triangles $\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K\to\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]\to$ (their spectral sequences are those of [def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations], the first one with the exact functor $g^{-1}$ applied): thus $D^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Phi\,\tau_{\leq q}K)$, $E^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Phi(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]))$, the map $\alpha:D^{p,q}\to D^{p-1,q+1}$ is induced by $\tau_{\leq q}K\to\tau_{\leq q+1}K$, likewise for $D',E',\alpha'$ with $\Phi'$, and the morphism of exact couples $(t_D,t_E)$ given there by the exchange morphisms has $t_D^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Ex_{\square,\tau_{\leq q}K})$. Fix $n\in\mathbf Z$. Then:

1. Both couples satisfy the hypotheses of [thm-sp-half-plane-convergence] ($D^{p,q}=0$ for $q<a$, and $E^{p,q}=0$ unless $p\geq0$ and $q\geq a$); so their spectral sequences converge to the canonical abutments $A^n=D^{0,n}$, $A'^n=D'^{0,n}$, with the finite filtrations $F^pA^n$, $F^pA'^n$ [def-sp-filtration] constructed there and $E_\infty^{p,n-p}\cong\operatorname{gr}^pA^n$, $E'^{p,n-p}_\infty\cong\operatorname{gr}^pA'^n$.
2. The maps $\iota_n:A^n=\mathcal H^n(\Phi\,\tau_{\leq n}K)\to\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)$ and $\iota'_n:A'^n\to\mathcal H^n(\Phi'K)$ induced by $\tau_{\leq n}K\to K$ are isomorphisms, and they carry $F^pA^n$ onto
$$F^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\mathcal H^n(\Phi\,\tau_{\leq n-p}K)\to\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)\bigr)$$
and $F^pA'^n$ onto the analogous $F^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi'K)$ (image filtrations [def-sp-image-filtration] induced by $\tau_{\leq n-p}K\to K$). Here $\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)=\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}Rf_*K)\cong g^{-1}\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)$, and this isomorphism carries $F^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)$ to $g^{-1}$ of the image of $\mathcal H^n(Rf_*\tau_{\leq n-p}K)\to\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)$.
3. $\iota'_n\circ t_D^{0,n}=\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K})\circ\iota_n$: under these identifications the map induced on the abutments by the morphism of exact couples is
$$\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K}):g^{-1}\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)\longrightarrow\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K).$$
4. $\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K})$ maps $F^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)$ into $F^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi'K)$ for every $p$, and the induced map $\operatorname{gr}^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)\to\operatorname{gr}^p\mathcal H^n(\Phi'K)$ is, under the identifications of (1) and (2), the map $E_\infty^{p,n-p}\to E'^{p,n-p}_\infty$ induced by the morphism of exact couples [lem-sp-couple-morphism].

proof.text: Step 1 (vanishing and convergence). For either additive composite F, lower cohomological bounds are preserved: right derived direct image has negative vanishing, and exact inverse image commutes with cohomology. For q<a the upper truncation is zero, since its cohomology vanishes both above q and below a; the layer H^q(K)[-q] is also zero. For p<0, the layer is bounded below by q, so H^(p+q) of its F-image vanishes. Transport these statements through the supplied D/E identifications and apply halfPlaneConvergence to P and Q. Retain its actual limiting subobjects, normalized diagonal colimits, convergence, finite exhaustive separated filtrations, and canonical infinite-page comparisons.

Step 2 (canonical abutment isomorphisms). Apply the already proved source-library theorem DerivedCategory.Plus.isIso_homologyFunctor_map_map_truncLEι_app from WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.PlusDevissage to each composite, using the lower-bound preservation proved in Step 1. The maps H^n(F(truncLE_(n-p) K)) -> H^n(F K), with the total-degree transports, form a diagonal cocone: compatibility is the truncation inclusion equation followed by functoriality. The diagonal colimit gives its universal map. Its composite with the normalized zeroth cocone leg is the canonical truncation map, which is an isomorphism; the zeroth leg is itself an isomorphism by normalization. Thus the universal map is an isomorphism, heterogeneously equal to the canonical map, with the required formula at every leg.

Step 3 (transported image filtrations). Define U and V as the images of the diagonal image filtrations under the abutment isomorphisms. The image of image(A.ι p) followed by i is image(A.ι p followed by i), since factorThruImageSubobject is epic. Substitute the cocone-leg formulas from Step 2 and remove the isomorphisms on the sources; this gives precisely the canonical truncation-image formulas for every integer p, including negative p. Naturality of the inverse-image/cohomology isomorphism identifies the first formula with the image under the exact inverse-image functor. Factor the original cohomology map through its image, and use preservation of epimorphisms and functoriality to identify that image with inverse image of its original image subobject.

Step 4 (exchange and filtration maps). Transport the canonical tD and tE through the supplied D/E equalities. The three squares in truncation_exchange_couple_morphism produce a CoupleMorphism from P to Q, using the supplied heterogeneous identifications of alpha, f and g. Naturality of exchange at each canonical truncation inclusion gives (A.ι p followed by i) followed by H^n(exchange_K) = tD followed by (B.ι p followed by j). At p=0, normalize the two cocone legs to obtain the required abutment square. At every p, imageSubobjectMap of this square gives the map U.step p -> V.step p. Monicity of the target step inclusion proves compatibility with the successive-step inclusions; cokernel.map then gives the stated graded maps and their cokernel equations.

Step 5 (limiting cycles and graded compatibility). Apply derivedCoupleFunctoriality to the CoupleMorphism of Step 4 and to the same limiting subobjects L and M chosen in Step 1. Its maps on limiting cycles and their cokernels give z and tInf with the required inclusion and quotient equations. By the factor-through-cycle equation and the g square, toPageInfinity followed by tInf equals tD followed by toPageInfinity. The isomorphism i induces isomorphisms on every filtration step, hence cokernel.mapIso gives an isomorphism on every graded piece; likewise j. Compose these with the canonical infinite-page comparisons of Step 1, transporting p+(n-p)=n, to obtain e and e-prime with their prescribed comparison formulas. Cancel the epimorphism toPageInfinity supplied by convergence. The resulting square is the factorThruImageSubobject form of the naturality square in Step 4, followed by the quotient map, so it commutes by the image-map and cokernel-map equations. This proves the final graded compatibility.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
In total degree $n$, the two exact couples have only the finite row range
$a\leq q\leq n$. Their induced abutment map is the cohomology map

$$
\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}Rf_*K)\longrightarrow
\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K)
$$

of the derived exchange morphism, with the image filtrations of Definition
[def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations].
blueprint_sketch.proof:
On $\mathcal E_1^{p,q}$ one has $p\geq0$ and $q\geq a$. The equality
$p+q=n$ therefore forces $a\leq q\leq n$. On a hypercover total complex,
only these finitely many filtered quotients contribute to degree $n$.
Consequently direct-sum and product totalization agree in that degree, the
filtration is finite and separated, and passage from a finite skeleton to
the full hypercover changes none of its graded terms.

The maps $e_q:A_q\to B_q$ commute with
$\tau_{\leq q}K\to K$. For $q\geq n$, the omitted cohomology sheaves of
$K$ have degrees greater than $n$; after a nonnegative right-derived
functor they cannot contribute to total degree $n$. Hence

$$
\mathcal H^n(A_q)\xrightarrow{\sim}
\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}Rf_*K),\qquad
\mathcal H^n(B_q)\xrightarrow{\sim}
\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K).
$$

Under these identifications, $\mathcal H^n(e_q)$ is
$\mathcal H^n(\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,K})$ by naturality of exchange in
the truncation map. Its filtration is the image of
$\mathcal H^n(A_q)$ and maps to the image of $\mathcal H^n(B_q)$, exactly
the two filtrations defined earlier. Thus the exact-couple abutment map is
the specified derived exchange map, rather than an unnamed filtered
isomorphism.

The statement is restated self-contained in four claims: (1) both couples satisfy the hypotheses of thm-sp-half-plane-convergence, (2) the canonical abutments D^{0,n} are identified with H^n(Phi K), H^n(Phi' K) by tau_{<=n}K -> K, carrying the half-plane filtration to the image filtration of H^n(Phi tau_{<=n-p}K) (and, for Phi, to g^{-1} of the filtration of def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations), (3) under these the abutment map t_D^{0,n} is H^n(Ex_{square,K}), (4) it respects the filtrations and induces the E_infinity map on gr (lem-sp-couple-morphism, transported). [def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations] is

$$

$$

[def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples].

[def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples], their terms $D^{p,q}$ vanish

negative cohomology. Thus the hypotheses of the half-plane convergence theorem
hold for both couples. By the couple-morphism lemma, their morphism induces,
for every $n$, a map of the abutments of the two spectral sequences of
[def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations] respecting their filtered
structures. The abutments are $\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}Rf_*K)$ and $\mathcal
H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K)$ with the image filtrations supplied by the truncation
triangles of [def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples]. More
explicitly, the canonical abutment is $D^{0,n}$, and its map is the component

[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] to $\tau_{\leq n}K$. Both functors carry
$\tau_{\geq n+1}K$ to complexes with no cohomology in degrees $\leq n$, so the
truncation triangle identifies these $D^{0,n}$ terms with the displayed
degree-$n$ cohomology of the whole complexes. Naturality of exchange in
$\tau_{\leq n}K\to K$ identifies $t_D^{0,n}$ with $\mathcal
H^n(\Ex_{\square,K})$, as required.

On $\mathcal E_1^{p,q}$ one has $p\geq0$ and $q\geq a$. The equality
$p+q=n$ therefore forces $a\leq q\leq n$. On a hypercover total complex,
only these finitely many filtered quotients contribute to degree $n$.
Consequently direct-sum and product totalization agree in that degree, the
filtration is finite and separated, and passage from a finite skeleton to
the full hypercover changes none of its graded terms.

The maps $e_q:A_q\to B_q$ commute with
$\tau_{\leq q}K\to K$. For $q\geq n$, the omitted cohomology sheaves of
$K$ have degrees greater than $n$; after a nonnegative right-derived
functor they cannot contribute to total degree $n$. Hence

$$
\mathcal H^n(A_q)\xrightarrow{\sim}
\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}Rf_*K),\qquad
\mathcal H^n(B_q)\xrightarrow{\sim}
\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K).
$$

Under these identifications, $\mathcal H^n(e_q)$ is
$\mathcal H^n(\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,K})$ by naturality of exchange in

isomorphism.
